headline: Fuel Prices Rise September 8: Gasoline +₱4.69, Diesel +₱5.18, Kerosene +₱5.58 per Liter
seoTitle: Fuel Prices Rise September 8: DOE Confirms New Rates | FMB News
seoDescription: Philippine fuel prices will increase on September 8, 2026: gasoline by ₱4.69/L, diesel by ₱5.18/L and kerosene by ₱5.58/L, according to the Department of Energy.
deck: The Department of Energy confirmed substantial pump-price increases effective September 8: ₱4.69 per liter for gasoline, ₱5.18 for diesel and ₱5.58 for kerosene.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The Department of Energy confirmed that Philippine pump prices will rise on Tuesday, September 8, following last week’s rollback.

Gasoline will increase by ₱4.69 per liter across the grades cited by the DOE, diesel by ₱5.18 per liter and kerosene by ₱5.58 per liter. GMA News reported the confirmed adjustments on September 7, while the Philippine News Agency independently published the same three figures ahead of implementation.
These are confirmed price adjustments, not the earlier market estimates that had projected increases in roughly the ₱4-to-₱5 range.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The confirmed increases follow renewed pressure in international oil markets. Earlier industry estimates cited heightened Middle East tensions and risks to energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz, alongside tight diesel inventories and refinery disruptions, as factors pushing regional product prices higher.

The previous week brought domestic price cuts, making the September 8 adjustment a reversal for motorists. Actual retail prices will still vary by brand, station and location because the announced changes are per-liter adjustments rather than a single nationwide pump price.

sections.heading: Why this matters to Filipinos
paragraphs: The increases directly raise fuel costs for households, motorists, public-transport operators and businesses that depend on road freight. Diesel is particularly important to logistics and transport, so a large increase can also add cost pressure beyond the fuel station if sustained.

Consumers should distinguish the announced adjustment from claims about future inflation or fare increases. Those secondary effects are not automatic and depend on how long higher fuel costs persist, how businesses respond and whether government regulators approve any regulated fare changes.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch pump implementation beginning September 8 and any company-specific effective times or station-level differences. The next weekly adjustment will depend on subsequent international product prices and foreign-exchange movements.

FMB News will also watch Department of Energy updates on supply conditions and whether continued Middle East disruption materially changes the domestic outlook beyond this confirmed one-week adjustment.
